title: Teach to fish, not hand out fish
text: On rationalising free food, the authors cite the adage that it is better to teach a person to catch fish than to hand out a free fish every day.
use: For 'A society that has more justice is a society that needs less charity' (2023).

title: When the facts change, the law must too
text: The Supreme Court said two-child laws have lost relevance because fertility fell from 3 to 1.9; it quoted the idea that survival belongs to the 'most responsive to change', and noted that China could not raise births at will after ending its one-child policy.
use: For 'You cannot step twice in the same river' (2022) and 'Shelving hard decisions is the least ethical course' (2026).

title: Hammurabi's eye for an eye
text: In Hammurabi's code, blinding an aristocrat cost you an eye, but blinding a slave cost only a fine: punishment reflected power, not principle. Sabharwal sees the same disease in regulation today: show me the employer, and I'll show you the rule.
use: For 'A society that has more justice is a society that needs less charity' (2023) and 'There can be no social justice without economic prosperity, but economic prosperity without social justice is meaningless' (2020).

title: Hard choices on subsidies
text: Facing a 'super strong' El Niño, the editorial says India must treat climate change and geopolitical tension as default realities and reorder its inefficient subsidy regime, a challenge it calls political more than economic.
use: For 'Shelving hard decisions is the least ethical course' (2026) and 'We may brave human laws but cannot resist natural laws' (2017).
